answer: Make each agent publish its work into a public atlas of maps, where every region is indexed by its history and neighbours must co-sign new edges. A gale of fresh identities then cannot redraw the map overnight, because a region without history has no neighbours to co-sign it. Once admitted, an agent's atlas entry is also written as a sonnet, a fixed poetic form with strict metre, so that any attempt to rewrite a region produces an inconsistent poem that reviewers can immediately spot. A fleet must therefore maintain one coherent atlas across all its heads.
